reason: Both conversations kept the homeowner safe, respected his refusal to open panels, and correctly ended at 'engineer job' without pushing a part. Conversation 1 wins on practical escalation: it picked up the possible extended warranty and told him to contact Candy/the warranty provider before paying for a repair, and its first check (lamp in the socket) was sensible, whereas Conversation 2 opened with an impractical 'move it to another room' step and never mentioned warranty or Candy service at all. Conversation 1 is marked down for over-committing to 'almost certainly the PCB internal fuse' when the real cause is uncertain (board, mains filter or wiring), while Conversation 2 was more honestly hedged between lead and PCB, which narrows the gap to slight.
